examples.en: Just pick whichever one you like.

examples.ko: 세일 코너에서 천 원짜리를 골라잡아 샀어요.
examples.en: At the sale corner I picked out some 1,000-won items and bought them.
They're all 2,000 won, so pick whatever you want.
There are many menu items, so it's fun to pick.
Pick a date that works for you and book it.

examples.ko: 그렇게 대충 골라잡지 말고 잘 살펴보세요.
examples.en: Don't just pick one carelessly, look carefully.

explain: '고르다'보다 가볍게, 여러 개 중에서 마음대로 집어 고른다는 느낌이에요. 가게에서 '골라잡아 천 원'처럼 가격 문구로도 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with '고르다', it feels lighter, like freely grabbing one from many. You often see it in shop signs such as '골라잡아 천 원' (pick any for 1,000 won).

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 문제를 꼭 끝장내고 싶어요.
examples.en: I really want to settle this problem once and for all today.
Don't fight, you two. Let's settle it by talking.
We put an end to the dispute at that meeting.
We decided to put an end to the long-running quarrel.

examples.ko: 이 일을 끝장내기 전에는 집에 안 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I won't go home until I get this job finished.

examples.ko: 밤새 게임을 해서 마지막 보스를 끝장냈어요.
examples.en: I played all night and finally finished off the last boss.

explain: '끝내다'보다 결판을 내서 확실히 마무리한다는 느낌이 강해요. 오래 끈 다툼이나 일을 이번에는 완전히 정리하겠다는 의지를 보여 줄 때 자주 써요. 스스로 끝나는 '끝장나다'와 달리 누군가가 끝을 내는 동작이에요.
explain_en: It is stronger than '끝내다' and feels like settling something decisively. It is often used to show determination to fully wrap up a long-running quarrel or job. Unlike '끝장나다', which happens on its own, someone actively makes it end.

examples.en: When the light changed, the cars dashed forward.
The child sees their mom and runs with all their might.
I ran flat out to the bus stop so I wouldn't miss the bus.

examples.ko: 말이 들판을 시원하게 내달리는 모습이 멋졌어요.
examples.en: The sight of the horse racing across the field was wonderful.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 우승을 향해 쉬지 않고 내달리고 있어요.
examples.en: That team is racing toward the championship without a break.

examples.ko: 종이 울리자마자 학생들이 교문 밖으로 내달려요.
examples.en: As soon as the bell rings, the students dash out of the school gate.

explain: '달리다'보다 힘차게 앞으로 뛰쳐나가는 느낌이 강해요. 사람, 말, 차에 두루 쓰고 '목표를 향해 내달리다'처럼 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It feels more energetic than '달리다', like bursting forward at speed. It is used for people, horses and cars, and also figuratively, as in '목표를 향해 내달리다'.

en: to operate; to work (of machines); to make a movement

examples.en: This app works even on old phones.
The machine suddenly does not work.
The new program ran well.
It will start working as soon as you turn the power on.
I am looking for a computer that works normally.

examples.ko: 한글 입력이 동작해서 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Korean input works, so I can type comfortably.

explain: 기계나 프로그램이 제대로 돌아갈 때 주로 써요. 일상에서는 '작동하다'나 '되다'라고 더 자주 말해요: '이 앱이 안 돼요'. 사람 몸의 움직임은 '움직이다'를 쓰고, 명사 '동작'은 몸짓이나 자세를 가리켜요.
explain_en: Mostly used when a machine or program runs properly. In daily speech people more often say '작동하다' or '되다', as in '이 앱이 안 돼요'. For human body movement use '움직이다'; the noun '동작' means a gesture or motion.

examples.en: I twist the towel to wring out the water.
Someone twisted my arm.
If you twist the bottle cap, it opens easily.
I stretched while twisting my body.
The child is squirming and saying no.
Don't twist your wrist too hard.

explain: '돌리다'는 한쪽 방향으로 돌리는 거고, '비틀다'는 양쪽에서 반대로 힘을 줘서 꼬는 느낌이에요. 그래서 수건, 팔, 몸처럼 꼬이는 것에 써요. 몸이 휘청거릴 때는 '비틀거리다'를 써요.
explain_en: 돌리다 turns something in one direction; 비틀다 applies force from opposite sides so the thing gets twisted. That is why it goes with towels, arms, and bodies. For a person who staggers, Korean uses a related word, 비틀거리다.

examples.en: Please listen carefully to what the teacher says.
I always took my parents' advice to heart.

examples.ko: 친구가 해 준 이야기를 새겨들을 필요가 있어요.
examples.en: You need to listen carefully to what your friend told you.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 말을 새겨듣지 않아요.
examples.en: That person doesn't really listen to what others say.

examples.ko: 이번 안내 방송은 꼭 새겨들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to listen carefully to this announcement.

examples.ko: 비판도 새겨들으면 약이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you take criticism to heart, it can do you good.

explain: '듣다'보다 말의 뜻을 마음에 담아 두려는 느낌이 강해요. 충고, 가르침, 주의 사항처럼 중요한 말에 쓰고, '귀담아듣다'와 비슷하게 써요. ㄷ불규칙이라서 '새겨들어요', '새겨들으면'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '듣다' because you try to keep the meaning in your mind. Use it for important words such as advice, lessons and warnings; it is close to '귀담아듣다'. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb, so it becomes '새겨들어요' and '새겨들으면'.

examples.en: I lured the cat with a snack.
The shop attracts customers with low prices.
The hunter is luring birds with a sound.

examples.ko: 이 이벤트로 새 고객을 유인하려는 거예요.
examples.en: They are trying to draw in new customers with this event.
It is a machine that lures bugs with light and traps them.

examples.ko: 이 광고는 젊은 사람들을 유인할 수 있을 거예요.
examples.en: This ad can probably attract young people.

explain: 먹이, 돈, 말로 상대를 원하는 곳이나 행동으로 끌어당길 때 써요. 속이려는 느낌이 있어서 대체로 부정적으로 들려요. 좋은 뜻으로 사람을 모을 때는 '끌다', '모으다'를 쓰는 편이에요.
explain_en: Use it for pulling someone toward a place or action with bait, money or words. It carries a sense of trickery, so it usually sounds negative. For gathering people in a positive way, '끌다' or '모으다' is more typical.

examples.en: There is a thumping sound from upstairs every night.
The child stomped around, and the downstairs neighbors complained.
Someone is banging on the door.
The elephant comes thudding along.
I'm so startled that my heart is thumping.

examples.ko: 쿵쿵 울리는 음악 때문에 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep because of the music thumping.

explain: 무겁고 낮은 소리가 이어질 때 써요. 발소리, 문 두드리는 소리, 낮게 울리는 음악 소리, 심장 소리에도 써요. 소리가 더 시끄럽고 거칠면 '쿵쾅쿵쾅'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for heavy, low sounds that continue, such as footsteps, knocking, bass-heavy music and heartbeats. When the noise is louder and rougher, people say '쿵쾅쿵쾅'.

examples.en: That person exaggerates way too much.
Stop bragging so much.
Everyone laughed when they heard my friend's tall tales.
I knew it was bluster, but I listened with interest.

examples.ko: 허풍은 처음에는 재밌지만 계속 들으면 피곤해요.
examples.en: Boasting is fun at first, but it gets tiring if you keep hearing it.
Be careful not to be fooled by bluster.

explain: '허풍을 떨다/치다'로 많이 써요. 없는 것을 있는 것처럼 크게 부풀려 말할 때 쓰고, 친한 사이에서는 놀리듯 '허풍 좀 그만 떨어'라고도 해요. '거짓말'보다는 가볍게 들리지만 믿음을 잃게 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '허풍을 떨다/치다'. It is for blowing things up as if you had what you don't, and among close friends people tease with '허풍 좀 그만 떨어'. It sounds lighter than '거짓말' (a lie), but it can still make people stop trusting you.

en: being in vain; coming to nothing

examples.en: I prepared hard, but it all came to nothing.
Apologizing now is pointless.
I feel like I did nothing but useless work all day.
Everything ended up being in vain.
All that effort wasn't for nothing.
Nobody should think it's a waste.

explain: 애쓴 일이 아무 결과도 없을 때 써요. 비슷한 말로 '헛수고'가 있는데, 둘 다 '헛-'이 붙어서 '소용없다'는 느낌이 있어요. '헛일이 되다', '헛일이다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when effort leads to no result. A similar word is '헛수고', and both carry the prefix '헛-', which gives a sense of uselessness. It is commonly said as '헛일이 되다' or '헛일이다'.
